claims.text: Elemental Ti in CoCrFeNiTi is prone to forming brittle HCP and Laves phases during conventional casting.
Conventionally cast CoCrFeNiTi has high porosity and a soft, single-phase FCC structure.
The proposed process uses high-energy milling at 400 rpm for 4–6 h followed by SPS at 1050–1100 °C and 30–40 MPa, with a heating rate above 50 °C/min and a dwell below 10 min.
High-energy milling followed by rapid SPS under the proposed conditions will suppress porosity in CoCrFeNiTi.
The proposed process will produce a nanocrystalline grain size below 100 nm.
The resulting CoCrFeNiTi structure will be an FCC-dominant solid solution with a minor BCC fraction.
Rapid processing will avoid HCP and Laves-phase formation in CoCrFeNiTi.
A macroscopic sintering strain rate below approximately 10^-3 s^-1 prevents Ti segregation.
Suppressing Ti diffusion prevents nucleation of HCP and Laves phases while stabilizing the FCC/BCC solid solution.
A high heating rate and short dwell limit the time available for Ti segregation.
Nb addition to CoCrFeNi can form a hard, brittle Co2Nb-type HCP Laves phase, associated with strongly negative mixing enthalpies between Nb and the constituent transition metals.
The Nb-based Laves-phase behavior is applicable to Ti-containing CoCrFeNiTi.
Defects introduced by high-energy milling lower the activation energy for FCC/BCC solid-solution formation.
Rapid SPS kinetically traps metastable FCC/BCC before CoCrFeNiTi equilibrates to brittle HCP.
The processed alloy will have less than 1% porosity.
The processed alloy will exceed 400 HV and have higher yield strength than cast counterparts.
Temperatures above 1150 °C or sufficiently long dwell times allow Ti segregation and HCP/Laves-phase formation.
FCC remains metastable in the relevant CoCrFeNiTi regime when Ti is below approximately 15 at.%.
Vickers testing at a 500 g load and 15 s dwell is an applicable hardness measurement condition for ball-milled, SPS-processed CoCrFeNi-based alloys.
Absence of load-dependent nanoindentation hardness decisively indicates absence of a grain-size strengthening effect and distinguishes it from solute strengthening.

contradictions.description: The operating regime requires a heating rate greater than 50 °C/min, but the rapid-sintering test group uses exactly 50 °C/min and therefore does not test the stated regime.

The boundary says the hypothesis holds if the dwell time exceeds 15 min, while the same sentence says such extended conditions permit segregation; elsewhere the required dwell is below 10 min. The boundary likely intended 'does not exceed 15 min.'

The proposed hardness comparison does not directly require verification that Group A and Group B have different grain sizes. Thus, similar hardness cannot by itself contradict the claimed grain-refinement mediator, and load-dependent indentation hardness is not uniquely attributable to grain size.
